March 1944 community placed under house arrest; early May taken to the Kecskemét ghetto; early June deported to Auschwitz. Rabbi Dr. Josef Klein (1933-1944) perished.
From 22 May 1944 more than 500 Cegléd Jews were concentrated in a small ghetto of 28 yellow-star houses; 17 June 1944 moved to the Kecskemét collection camp, end of June deported to Auschwitz.
670 people deported in 1944; 540 became Holocaust victims, 130 survived (deportation/victim counts, not a resident census).
